historical_record.description: The Alvord Lake Bridge was built — the first reinforced-concrete bridge in the United States, and a National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark.
Commissioner William Alvord gave $200 for a lily pond opposite Haight Street, stocked with hardy water lilies as an experiment.
The pond in the valley opposite the Haight Street depot was by now called Alvord Lake, with an archway under the carriage drive planned to lead from it into the children's grounds.
The Market Street Cable Railway Company paid for the passage under the main drive leading from the Haight Street entrance into the Children's Quarters.
The lake was doubled in size and reshaped with bold rocky points, then planted with bamboo, weeping willows and other waterside plants, for $726.50.
